problem: Existing VLN agents ignore common house-layout regularities (e.g., bathrooms next to bedrooms) and only reason over visible regions, so they generalize poorly to unseen environments. Prior ego-centric map methods map only visible regions, use few room classes, and were not tested on long-horizon VLN.
motivation: Humans use layout priors to predict nearby rooms in new homes. Giving agents a compact prediction of neighboring room types and directions, including occluded but adjacent rooms, could narrow the seen/unseen gap and cut down candidate actions.
key_idea: Train a locality predictor on room-adjacency knowledge mined from HM3D to predict an ego-centric neighbourhood room-type map, lift it to an imagined global grid, and feed it as target tokens to a cross-modal transformer for action selection.
insight: Locality map quality drives performance: with the 5x5 map, random room types and directions give 31.40 SR, predicted maps 72.29, and ground-truth locality 78.22 on R2R ValUnseen, so the prior is genuinely used. The map should span only about two average rooms; SR peaks at 5x5 (72.29) and drops at 7x7 (61.38) and 9x9 (51.33). Because only room-to-room relations are modelled, REVERIE navigation improves but object grounding (RGS/RGSPL) does not.
method: Locality Knowledge base: builds a one-viewpoint-per-room dataset from unannotated HM3D by sampling viewpoints at least 2 m apart, filtering by ORB matches, and labelling room types with a ResNet trained on MP3D. Adjacency (shared wall), visibility and navigability are deduced to form a ground-truth locality map M^GT.
Locality map: a g×g grid (cell 0.5 m) around the agent that encodes room type, orientation and distance relative to agent heading.

Locality Predictor: an egocentric mapper projects panoramic visual features to the ground plane with a MapNet-style height-wise max. A map decoder (concatenation of M_{t-1} and M_t, then an LSTM with the previous action embedding) extends this to occluded neighbours, and it is trained with cross-entropy against M^GT.

Target Encoder: converts the ego-centric prediction to the global frame with a rigid-body transform. The Imaginary Scene Tokenization from TD-STP gives position tokens, and the room type, orientation and distance features are added to form target tokens c_t.

WIN cross-modal transformer: adapted from HAMT/TD-STP, it attends over language (BERT), panoramic vision, history and target tokens. The [CLS] embedding feeds an MLP that gives a probability over candidate viewpoints, and a global target is decoded from the target tokens.

Training: the locality predictor is trained first and then frozen. The VLN agent is trained with IL (teacher action plus history teacher loss) combined with A2C RL, with reward for distance reduction and stopping within 3 m. WIN+VLN-BERT simply multiplies the global map prediction into the action probabilities.

setting.backbone: HAMT/TD-STP-style cross-modal transformer with BERT language encoder plus LSTM locality predictor (trained); also a Recurrent VLN-BERT variant
setting.training_data: R2R / REVERIE training splits, plus a locality knowledge set mined from the 900 unannotated HM3D houses; the room classifier is a ResNet trained on MP3D. TD-STP itself uses augmented data.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB-D (36 views, 3 elevations) plus relative heading/elevation
setting.simulator: Matterport3D simulator (R2R/REVERIE); HM3D used for locality data
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT locality map used only in an upper-bound ablation)

numbers.extra: single-run; TD-STP base uses augmented data

numbers_note: The grid-size and map-type ablations report R2R ValUnseen SR of 72.29 and SPL 64.37 for the 5x5 predicted map, slightly different from the 72/64 in Table 1. The abstract's '68% SR / 63% SPL in unseen' matches the R2R test-unseen row.
results: WIN+STP reaches R2R val-unseen SR 72 / SPL 64 and test-unseen SR 68 / SPL 63, improving on TD-STP (test SR 67 / SPL 61) and matching EnvEdit's SR of 68. On REVERIE test-unseen SR rises from 35.89 to 42.19 over TD-STP, but it remains far below DUET (52.51), and grounding scores do not improve.
limitations: Performance degrades on trajectories with uncommon or uncorrelated room types, and the agent can get stuck when locality contradicts the vision-language action prediction.
Only room-to-room relations are modelled, with no object-to-room relations, so REVERIE grounding (RGS/RGSPL) does not improve and DUET is much stronger.
Locality knowledge comes from noisy automatic labels on HM3D, and the useful map size is limited to about two rooms (5x5 grid).
